content.text:
Here are some notable **art collaborations from 2023**, especially where contemporary art crossed into fashion, design, luxury, and public-facing culture:

| Collaboration | What it was | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| **Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama** | A major 2023 capsule across bags, ready-to-wear, shoes, fragrances, store installations, and global campaigns using Kusama’s polka dots, pumpkins, flowers, and mirrored motifs. | One of the year’s biggest art–fashion collaborations, reviving LV and Kusama’s earlier 2012 partnership. ([fashionista.com](https://fashionista.com/2023/01/louis-vuitton-yayoi-kusama-collaboration-collection-prices-2023?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Louis Vuitton Artycapucines 2023** | The fifth Artycapucines collection invited artists including **Billie Zangewa, Ewa Juszkiewicz, Liza Lou, Tursic & Mille, and Ziping Wang** to reinterpret the Capucines handbag. | Continued LV’s collector-oriented model of turning a luxury object into an artist-edition piece. ([vanityfair.com](https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2023/10/louis-vuittons-fifth-iteration-of-artycapucines-has-arrived?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Fashion houses x contemporary artists** | 2023 saw continued momentum around fashion-art capsules, with publications highlighting Louis Vuitton x Kusama as one of the year’s most anticipated collaborations. | Shows how art collaborations became central to luxury marketing and cultural relevance in 2023. ([ww.fashionnetwork.com](https://ww.fashionnetwork.com/news/The-most-anticipated-fashion-collabs-of-2023%2C1472920.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Harvard Art Museums x metaLAB / AI collaboration** | The project **“Surprise Machines”** used AI and experimental museology to visualize Harvard Art Museums’ image collection of over 200,000 objects. | A museum-tech-art collaboration exploring AI as a curatorial and discovery tool. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09343?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Artists x AI-protection researchers: Glaze** | Researchers and artists collaborated on **Glaze**, a tool designed to protect artists’ styles from being mimicked by text-to-image AI models. | One of 2023’s most important art-tech collaborations, responding to generative AI’s impact on artists. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04222?utm_source=openai)) |

If you mean **brand collaborations with artists**, the biggest 2023 example was definitely **Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama**. If you mean **artist-to-artist collaborations**, **museum collaborations**, or **music/visual art collaborations**, I can make a more targeted list.
